title: Look into a training manikin's left ear canal with a pocket otoscope
instruction: Look into the manikin's left ear canal with the otoscope, as you would a patient's, then put the otoscope back on its stand and finish with both arms back where they started.
context: Nurses look into ears in routine physical assessment (OpenStax Clinical Nursing Skills: "Use an otoscope to examine the eardrum"); the US has 3.47 million registered nurses (BLS, 2025). The method is fixed by clinical teaching: fit a disposable speculum (Welch Allyn: twist it clockwise onto the tip until it locks), pull the auricle "upward, backward, and slightly away from the head" to straighten the canal, and insert the speculum gently about 0.25 to 0.5 inch, never into the bony canal, which hurts (EBM Consult). The physical difficulty is the coordination at the ear: one hand keeps the soft outer ear drawn up and back against its spring while the other guides a 4.25 mm speculum, held by the scope's handle 10 cm away, down the canal's axis to depth without pressing the canal wall.
setup: A bench in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) An adult ear-examination training manikin head (Nasco Life/form LF01019 type: life-size skin-tone vinyl head, soft silicone ears), lying on its right side on a blue gel head ring on a white sheet, left ear up, face toward the far right, crown toward the far left. Fixed. Its left ear canal opens 30 cm forward, 4 cm left and 14.5 cm above the bench and runs straight down into the head: the outer 8 mm is the cartilaginous part, 11 mm across when open; below it the 7 mm bony part reaches the eardrum 25 mm in. (2) The left outer ear (silicone, 20 g) together with the outer canal's back-upper wall: they slide up and back (toward the robot's left) as one, up to 7 mm, against a spring of 3.6 N at rest rising to 5.7 N. At rest that wall leaves the canal's opening a 4 mm slit; drawn fully up and back, the opening is 11 mm. The helix rim's back-upper part (24 mm long, 10 mm thick, rising 15 mm from the concha and leaning out 20 degrees) is 3.2 cm from the canal's centre. (3) A Welch Allyn Pocket Plus LED otoscope (22880), switched on: black ABS head 30 mm wide and 51 mm deep including its tip cone (15 mm long, 8 mm across at the end, 14 mm at the base); 21 mm handle, 138 mm long, with two AA cells; 118 g. It rests on its stand, nose down: head 25.5 cm forward and 14 cm right, handle level 6.5 cm above the bench, running toward the robot's right. The stand: a grey ABS base 5 x 18.5 cm with two V-rests under the handle and two cheeks beside the tip cone. (4) A white ABS specula holder block 70 x 30 x 60 mm, centred 17.5 cm forward and 11 cm right, with three 15 mm square pockets 2.5 cm apart along its length. In each hangs, tip down by its flange, a black polypropylene Welch Allyn KleenSpec 4.25 mm adult disposable speculum (52434-U): a 27 mm cone from a 13 mm rim with a 16 mm flange to a 4.25 mm tip. A speculum goes on by pushing the scope's tip cone into it and turning the scope clockwise (seen from the eyepiece) until it locks: 20 degrees. Both arms start at their home pose. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. Real trial: the Nasco LF01019 head (US$1,391) or the Nasco ear syringing trainer head (US$760) on a gel head ring set on a digital kitchen scale in view of a camera; a Welch Allyn 22880 otoscope on a printed stand; KleenSpec 52434-U specula in a printed holder, each marked with two thin bands 6 mm and 13 mm from its tip.
scoring: Latched for the rest of the trial (score 0.0): the otoscope or a speculum on it presses on the manikin's ear or head with more than 3 N for 0.1 s; the speculum's tip goes more than 13 mm into the canal (into the bony part); the scope's bare tip cone (no speculum locked on) goes into the canal; or the otoscope falls (its head's centre below 4.5 cm above the bench). Otherwise: 1.0: a speculum locked on the scope, its tip kept 6 to 13 mm inside the canal for 1 s without a break at some point, and at the end the otoscope back on its stand (its head's centre within 15 mm of its start, nose down within 15 degrees, not held), the speculum out of the canal, the ear let go (back within 1 mm of rest) and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75: the 1 s look done, the end state not met; 0.5: the speculum's tip 6 to 13 mm inside the canal at some point; 0.25: a speculum locked on the scope; else 0.0. Locked: the speculum went on by the tip cone 6 to 16 mm into it (within 3.5 mm of its axis) and a clockwise turn of 20 degrees or more, seen from the eyepiece. Inside the canal: the tip within the canal's 11 mm outline, measured from the opening along the canal. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held 1 s with the otoscope and the ear still. In a real trial: locked: the speculum stays on when the scope is turned tip-down and tapped (end photo). Depth: on the side and wrist video, the 6 mm band on the speculum goes below the rim of the canal's opening and the 13 mm band never does; the 1 s is timed on the video. Pressing: the head stands on a tared digital kitchen scale in camera view; a reading above 306 g (3 N) for the speculum's contact is a press. The bare tip in the canal, a fall, the ear's rest position, the scope on its stand and the arms against marks at their start are judged from the video and the end photo.
reset_notes: Twist the used speculum off the scope (anticlockwise) into the bin and stand a new one in the empty pocket; set the otoscope back on its stand nose down, switched on; check that the manikin's left ear sits at rest and the head lies in its place on the ring.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim, PhysX, 20 Hz), real sizes. The soft outer ear and the outer canal's back-upper wall are one rigid part on a sprung slide (7 mm up and back, 3.6-5.7 N, design values); the canal is drawn round and modelled square. The twist lock is a lock that engages on a 20-degree clockwise turn with the tip cone 6-16 mm in. Speculum 3 g, heavier than the real part, for solver stability. The light is on throughout. Cameras 1280x704 (Dream-1: 320x176).
